messages.author: f87814d7c9410bb4
messages.subject: detection function with covariate
parts:
Hello,

I am analysing line transect data using R. I have two doubts:

1. If I fit a detection function with two covariates (Package: Distance), may I use the same covariate in DSM again?? How it is going to affect the DSM results and variance?

2. I have two different observations in one segment therefore, 'Sample.Label' for two observations is identical. This is causing an error in abundance estimation in package 'Distance'. How to deal with this?

Many thanks in advance :)

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] detection function with covariate
parts:
Deepti

It is possible that environmental factors that affect detectability may also influence encounter rates; so it is plausible to use the same covariate in both the detection function model and the dsm model.  I'm not certain, but I don't think there are serious consequences of this for either point or interval estimates of abundance.  Someone with first-hand experience with this might have thoughts.

I don't understand the second question.  Segments are not equivalent to samples.  If you have used 'Sample.Label' column, the function ds() understands this to be the transect on which the detections were made.  It is very common for there to be >1 detection on a transect; ds() handles this without a problem.

Are you trying to estimate abundance with dsm or with ds? 

Eric Rexstad

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] detection function with covariate
parts:
Deepti

The error message is not related to number of detections per transect (I presume your use of 'segment' is equivalent to 'transect').  It is perfectly fine for there to be multiple detections on a transect.

The error message says there is a problem with the way in which you have labelled your transects ('Sample.Label').  Have you sorted your data such that all observations related to a transect appear together? I may be able to diagnose the problem more quickly if I knew the nature of your data.  Do you have more than one stratum in your data?

An alternative for organising your data is also possible.  Rather than employ region.table , sample.table , obs.table , if your data is in a suitable format, consult the help under ?flatfile in the Distance package.

Wishes
Deepti

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: detection function with covariate
parts:
Deepti

I'm not sure what you are attempting.  You have transects that you are transforming into "segments".  Then how are you trying to analyse the "segments"?  Are you treating them as if they were transects?  Not sure that is a good idea.

However, if what I have written is correct, then segment (which are being treated as if they were transects) will need to have effort associated with them in your flatfile (which perhaps you are calling 'distdata'?)
